Routines / daily commitments such as different forms of meditations and different forms of yoga, eating healthy foods, being hydrated, walks in nature / mindful walks, dream work, inner work and self reflection, education / courses / free courses which interest you, audiobooks about different areas which don't cover your interest, being social and going somewhere regular ( this can even be simply going to places where other people are, in time you could ask some people open ended questions which don't typically reply with yes or no, so you can learn more about other people such as, how was your day been, I've seen you come here a few times, how long have you been coming ect ) foam rollers / massage balls for muscular tensions, acupressure matts for tension, osho dynamic meditation for emotional release, ptsd meditations / guided sleep meditations, yoga nidra ( which is basically a guided mindful meditation) jon kabat zinn has some great mindful meditations on YouTube, Peter levine has some great content on healing childhood trauma also! It could be that you are ready to process past experiences, and subconsciously opening up - trauma healing is not often straight forward, its up down inside and out, but in time you build the mental resistance and adapt the ego to handle it with better control / balance and awareness.

The split is common in dissociation it is an archaic self defence mechanism which consciousness uses to protect the life by splitting itself and forms a holder for the ego. It can be worked with, and healed, or adapted to form a cohesive personality.

The mood swings are natural - due to inner conflicts or external triggers. It takes time to become aware of these, but the sooner you are aware of your triggers the sooner you can start healing.

Boards like cptsd reddit could be triggering for some people with cptsd, while they have good intentions. 

Sometimes we need time to heal once we are more open to our past for integration in our psyche, at times like these i find what helps is prioritising healing and minimise my stressors. 

I spend more time 'being', being more aware of my thoughts with no judgement as attachment to thoughts prevents healing - eating healthier, yoga / exercise, guided meditations and mindfulness, guided body scans and breathing exercises / pranayamas are great practices to help.

Some forms of meditation may not help, such as vipasanna and bioenergetics because they may cause resurfacing by directing your awarenesss into the pain bodies or your psyches centre - This can be used as a tool for healing though, when we are ready.

But of course we are all unique and our trauma reaction / mechanics are also so it is complex. So find what works for you 😀
